title: "Cash: money over time"
unit: 4

<Phase type="activation">

Picture crossing a river on stepping stones. The far bank is solid, and there are enough stones to reach it. But between the third and the fourth stone the gap is wider than a step.

**Profit is the far bank. Cash is the stones along the way.** Think about where in your retreat that wide gap might be.

</Phase>

<Phase type="reflection">

Go back to the stones. It does not matter how good the bank is if, in the middle of the river, there is nothing to step on.

**A profitable retreat can leave the leader with no money two months before arrival.** Not because of a bad price, but because of the order in which payments come in and go out.

</Phase>

<Phase type="concept">

## Profit and money in the account are different things

Honest profit counts everything at once, as if the retreat had already happened. Cash counts month by month: what came in, what went out, how much is left.

Guest payments come in as places sell. Venue payments go out under the contract: a first payment at signing, then installments or one large payment before arrival. When the second overtakes the first, the account goes negative. That is the cash gap.

## How venue payments work

Typical terms of group contracts:

- a first payment of 10 to 25 % of the contract at signing;
- the balance usually a week to a month before arrival, earlier at some venues;
- sometimes installments in equal parts up to the final payment.

The first payment is the hardest moment for a new leader. It has to be found before a single place is sold.

## The gap in the teaching deal

In the [teaching deal](https://academy.synergify.com/en/instrumenty/kalkulyator-retrita/#) the venue gets 25 % at signing and the balance in installments up to a final payment 60 days before. Guests pay 30 % on booking and the rest 45 days before. Sales run evenly, three or four places a month.

The calculator shows a gap of 17,028 dollars in the third month. Honest profit stays the same — 22,200.

## What closes the gap

Try one lever at a time in the calculator and watch the gap:

- **a bigger first guest payment:** 50 % instead of 30 — the gap falls to 8,880;
- **early sales:** all places in the first two months — 11,790;
- **a later final payment to the venue:** 30 days instead of 60 — 12,978;
- **no installments:** the venue balance in one payment before arrival — 5,508, and already in the month of signing.

The last item is a surprise. Installments are convenient for the venue. But for a leader with slow sales they can cost more than one payment.

**One rule closes almost everything: book the venue once first payments from the minimum group are in.** Then the first venue payment is paid with guests' money, not yours.

<SelfCheck id="c4"/>

</Phase>

<Phase type="practice">

1. Open the [teaching deal](https://academy.synergify.com/en/instrumenty/kalkulyator-retrita/#) and find the monthly cash plan.
2. Find the month where the balance is lowest and write down the amount.
3. Try each lever from the list above, one at a time. After each, restore the original value.
4. Choose two levers you could really use yourself and switch them on together.
5. Write down what gap remains and in which month. That is the sum you need to have before the first sale.

</Phase>
